title: Optimistic exploration and PAC-MDP sample complexity

items.title: Finite discounted MDP with bounded real rewards
items.statement: Let S be a nonempty finite state set, let each state s have a nonempty finite action set A(s), and let 0 ≤ gamma < 1. A bounded-reward finite discounted MDP assigns to each admissible (s,a) a probability measure K(·|s,a) on S × [0,1] with the discrete sigma-algebra on S and the Borel sigma-algebra on [0,1]. The next state and reward may be dependent. Write P(s'|s,a)=K({s'}×[0,1]|s,a) and r(s,a)=integral rho K(ds',d rho|s,a). A behavior is a sequence of probability kernels from observed-history spaces H_t, with finite-product sigma-algebras and Borel reward coordinates, to admissible actions at the current state.
items.strategy: Extend the existing finite-state/action MDP interface to general bounded Borel reward laws while retaining its joint next-state/reward convention.

items.title: Well-defined discounted values and optimal Bellman fixed points
items.statement: Assume AC. In any bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, the trajectory law for each history-dependent behavior and starting state exists, and its discounted return is integrable with value in [0,1/(1-gamma)]. For each stationary policy pi, V^pi satisfies its Bellman equation. The Bellman optimality operator T*V(s)=max over a in A(s) of [r(s,a)+gamma sum over s' P(s'|s,a)V(s')] is a gamma contraction with a unique fixed point V*. This fixed point is the supremum of values of all behaviors, is attained by a deterministic stationary greedy policy, and Q*(s,a)=r(s,a)+gamma sum over s' P(s'|s,a)V*(s') is the optimal action value.
items.strategy: Construct the history-dependent path law, use the geometric tail bound for discounted returns, and prove Bellman optimality by finite-horizon induction and contraction.

items.title: Concentration for adaptively sampled MDP observations
items.statement: Assume AC and fix a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP. For each state-action pair, expose an independent stream of joint next-state/reward outcomes and reveal the next unused outcome only on a visit; this coupling has the MDP trajectory law under any history-dependent behavior. At each deterministic sample size m, the reward mean satisfies P(|r_hat-r|>x)≤2 exp(-2mx^2), and the empirical next-state law satisfies E||p_hat-p||_1≤sqrt(S/m) and P(||p_hat-p||_1>sqrt(S/m)+sqrt(2 ln(1/delta)/m))≤delta. For any fixed filtration and m, bounded predictable variables Y_i in [0,B] satisfy P(|sum(Y_i-E[Y_i|F_{i-1}])|≥mx)≤2 exp(-2mx^2/B^2). At any finite adaptive visit count the next fixed-size unused block retains its conditional iid law; no uniform confidence bound at a data-dependent sample count is asserted.
items.strategy: Couple adaptive visits to independent potential streams, prove the empirical L1 expectation bound coordinatewise, and apply the conditional Hoeffding and Azuma suppliers.

items.title: PAC-MDP sample complexity of exploration
items.statement: Assume AC and fix a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, an initial state, and a learning algorithm as a history-dependent behavior. At time t≥1 let h_t end in state s_t and let A_t be the continuation of its action kernels after h_t. Define V^{A_t}(h_t) as the expected discounted return from that fixed history and N_epsilon=# {t≥1: V^{A_t}(h_t)<V*(s_t)-epsilon}, for epsilon≥0. For epsilon>0 and delta∈(0,1), a PAC-MDP bound B(S,A,epsilon,delta,gamma) satisfies P(N_epsilon≤B)≥1-delta for every MDP with S states and at most A actions per state and every initial state; no permanent-stopping condition is imposed.
items.strategy: Define the bad-step count from the algorithm's full continuation behavior and the optimal discounted value.

items.title: Admissible upper heuristic for a discounted MDP
items.statement: For a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, an admissible upper heuristic is a function U on admissible state-action pairs satisfying Q*(s,a) ≤ U(s,a). It is nonnegative. If V0 is any supplied upper bound for U with 0 ≤ V0 ≤ 1/(1-gamma), use the normalized bound Vmax=max(1,V0); then U(s,a) ≤ Vmax ≤ 1/(1-gamma). The normalization by 1 is used because sampled rewards are bounded by 1, even when all heuristic values are smaller.
items.strategy: State the action-value upper-bound hypothesis and normalize the scalar bound for the reward scale.

items.title: Value stability under empirical model error
items.statement: Let M1 and M2 be bounded-reward finite discounted MDPs on the same finite state/action domain with common gamma. If all stationary-policy and optimal values lie in [0,V] and reward/transition errors are alpha and beta uniformly, then all policy and optimal value differences are at most (alpha+gamma V beta)/(1-gamma). Here the finite-vector norms are max absolute coordinate and sum of absolute coordinates. Also, if all M1 policy/optimal values are at most 2W, M2 rewards lie in [0,1], and gamma beta≤(1-gamma)/2, then all policy and optimal value differences are at most 2(alpha+2 gamma W beta)/(1-gamma).
items.strategy: Subtract the Bellman fixed-point equations, bound the transition perturbation by V times its L1 error, and absorb the contraction term.

items.title: Known-state/action MDP with optimistic self-loops
items.statement: Let M be a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP, let K be a subset of its state-action pairs, and let q(s,a) lie in [0,Vmax] with Vmax ≤ 1/(1-gamma). The known-state/action MDP M_K(q) agrees with M on K. For each pair (s,a) outside K, add a distinct absorbing state with one action. The unknown pair transitions to that sink with reward (1-gamma)q(s,a), and the sink action self-loops with the same reward. The sink value is q(s,a), so the unknown pair's Bellman value is exactly q(s,a).
items.strategy: Replace each unknown pair by a self-loop whose reward encodes its current action value.

items.title: R-MAX with an admissible heuristic
items.statement: Input a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP interaction, gamma, an admissible heuristic U with normalized bound Vmax, an integer sample threshold m ≥ 1, an approximation tolerance beta in (0,1/(1-gamma)), and a total order on each A(s). Initialize every pair as unknown with Q(s,a)=U(s,a), count zero, and empty reward/next-state samples. Act greedily with the fixed tie order. Store only the first m observed rewards and next states of each pair. When a pair reaches m samples, mark it known, form its empirical reward mean and empirical next-state distribution, and rebuild Q by L value-iteration sweeps from Q0=0 for the operator H_K that uses the empirical Bellman backup on known pairs and U(s,a) on unknown pairs, where L=max(1,ceil(log(1/(beta(1-gamma)))/(1-gamma))). Continue until the next pair becomes known. The algorithm asserts no computational-time bound.
items.strategy: Define the empirical known-pair model, optimistic unknown-pair values, fixed tie-breaking, and the finite value-iteration approximation.

items.title: Delayed Q-learning with an admissible heuristic
items.statement: Initialize Q=U, batch sums zero, counts zero, batch starts zero, learning flags true, and last-update time zero. At each time choose a greedy action with fixed tie order and observe reward r and next state s'. If b(s,a)≤t*, enable learning. When learning, set b=t if the batch count is zero, increment the count, and add r+gamma max_c Q(s',c) to the batch sum. At count m, update Q(s,a) to the batch mean plus epsilon1 and set t*=t exactly when Q(s,a)-batchmean≥2epsilon1; otherwise disable learning exactly when b(s,a)>t*. Reset that pair's sum and count after each completed batch.
items.strategy: Specify the delayed Q-learning batch update, optimism bonus, and learn-flag reset rule using the standard tabular Q-learning target.

items.title: Escape-event reduction for optimistic greedy learning
items.statement: Assume AC. Let a greedy learner interact with a bounded-reward finite discounted MDP. Suppose B,W,Qc satisfy 0<B, 0<W≤1/(1-gamma), 0<Qc≤1/(1-gamma), and V*≤B. The learner maintains 0≤Q_t≤Qc and Q_t(s,a)≤W whenever (s,a) is outside its predictable known set K_t. Let V_t=max_a Q_t and pi_t be deterministic greedy. Assume K_t stays fixed except after a Q update or a selection outside K_t. Let M_t be the known-state/action MDP and C=B+W. If 0<eta≤C, eta(1-gamma)<1, and with probability at least 1-rho the conditions V_t≥V*-eta, V_t−V^{pi_t}_{M_t}≤eta for all times/states and total updates plus escapes≤zeta hold, then for 0<rho<1/2, with q=eta/(2C), H=1 if gamma=0 and otherwise max(1,ceil(ln(1/[eta(1-gamma)])/(-ln gamma))), and M=ceil((2(zeta+1)+2ln(1/rho))/q), one has P(N_{4eta}≤HM)≥1-2rho.
items.strategy: Compare the learned controller with the current greedy policy on the trap MDP over a logarithmic effective horizon, then count disjoint high-risk windows by conditional Bernoulli concentration.

items.title: Adaptive empirical-model accuracy for R-MAX
items.statement: Let 0<eta<Vmax/4 and 0<delta<1. Put b=eta(1-gamma)/(64Vmax), m=ceil(8(S+ln(8SA/delta))/b^2), and beta=eta(1-gamma)/16. With probability at least 1-delta, for every R-MAX known set, empirical/true trap-model policy and optimal values differ by at most eta/8, the Q table is within beta of empirical optimal action values and lies in [0,1/(1-gamma)], V_t≥V*-eta, V_t−V^{pi_t}_{M_K}≤eta, and total rebuild plus escape count is at most (m+1)|{(s,a):U(s,a)≥V*(s)-eta}|.
items.strategy: Use adaptive reward and transition concentration, the simulation lemma, admissible optimism, and value-iteration error to verify the escape theorem's hypotheses.

items.title: Delayed Q-learning optimism and update-count bounds
items.statement: Let D(s,a)=[U(s,a)-V*(s)]_+, kappa=ceil(SA Vmax/epsilon1), N=SA(1+kappa), C1=1+gamma Vmax, and m≥ceil(C1^2/(2epsilon1^2) ln(8N/delta)). With probability at least 1-delta, estimates remain optimistic, every attempted batch starting outside K_t={Q_t-r-gamma P V_t≤3epsilon1} succeeds, successful updates are at most G=sum_{s,a}(1+D(s,a)/epsilon1), and visits outside K_t are at most 2mG. The per-pair additive one is necessary even at zero slack.
items.strategy: Bound update attempts, apply conditional Hoeffding to each batch-start stream, prove optimism inductively, and charge escapes to successful updates.

items.title: PAC-MDP sample complexity of R-MAX
items.statement: For 0<epsilon<(1-gamma)^-1, 0<delta<1, and an admissible heuristic of cap Vmax, epsilon≥Vmax gives N_epsilon=0. Otherwise let eta=epsilon/4, b=eta(1-gamma)/(64Vmax), m=ceil(8(S+ln(16SA/delta))/b^2), beta=eta(1-gamma)/16, E_eta={(s,a):U(s,a)≥V*(s)-eta}, zeta=(m+1)|E_eta|, q=eta/(4Vmax), H=1 for gamma=0 and otherwise max(1,ceil(ln(1/[eta(1-gamma)])/(-ln gamma))), and M=ceil((2(zeta+1)+2ln(2/delta))/q). Then R-MAX with m and beta satisfies P(N_epsilon≤HM)≥1-delta. For U=Vmax=(1-gamma)^-1 this is O-tilde(S^2 A/[epsilon^3(1-gamma)^6]).
items.strategy: Verify optimism, empirical-model accuracy, greedy-policy accuracy, and the bounded number of unknown-pair visits, then apply the escape-event reduction.

items.title: PAC-MDP sample complexity of Delayed Q-learning
items.statement: For 0<epsilon<(1-gamma)^-1, 0<delta<1, and admissible heuristic cap Vmax, epsilon≥Vmax gives N_epsilon=0. Otherwise set eta=epsilon/4, epsilon1=eta(1-gamma)/3, kappa=ceil(SA Vmax/epsilon1), N=SA(1+kappa), C1=1+gamma Vmax, m=ceil(C1^2/(2epsilon1^2) ln(16N/delta)), D(s,a)=[U(s,a)-V*(s)]_+, G=sum(1+D/epsilon1), zeta=ceil((2m+1)G), q=eta/(4Vmax), H=1 for gamma=0 and otherwise max(1,ceil(ln(1/[eta(1-gamma)])/(-ln gamma))), and M=ceil((2(zeta+1)+2ln(2/delta))/q). Then Delayed Q-learning satisfies P(N_epsilon≤HM)≥1-delta. Up to logarithmic factors the bound is Vmax(1+gamma Vmax)^2[sum D+SA epsilon(1-gamma)]/[epsilon^4(1-gamma)^4]; the additive term remains at zero slack. For Vmax=(1-gamma)^-1 the leading order is O-tilde(SA/[epsilon^4(1-gamma)^8]).
items.strategy: Use the corrected per-pair update count, the high-probability optimism and residual events, and the escape-event reduction.

title: Optimistic exploration and PAC-MDP sample complexity — Examples

items.title: A finite bad-step count need not be a permanent stopping time
items.statement: In a one-state MDP with gamma=0, actions a and b give deterministic rewards 1 and 0. Fix n≥1 and let a controller choose b at times 1,...,n and n+2, and choose a at every other time. For epsilon=1/2 it has exactly n+1 bad steps, including a bad step after a good step, so the PAC-MDP count is not required to be a prefix of the run.
items.strategy: Evaluate each continuation behavior using gamma=0, then enumerate the bad time indices.

references.title: Alexander L. Strehl, Lihong Li, and Michael L. Littman, Reinforcement Learning in Finite MDPs: PAC Analysis
references.locator: §1.5, discussion after Definitions 1–2, PDF pp. 6–7 (printed p. 2418).

items.title: An inadmissible heuristic can suppress exploration forever
items.statement: In a one-state MDP with gamma=0, actions a and b give deterministic rewards 1 and 0, respectively. Set U(a)=U(b)=0 and use a tie order that selects b first. R-MAX then observes b only, keeps both unknown and known action values at 0, and chooses b forever, so for epsilon=1/2 every step is bad. The heuristic is inadmissible because U(a)<Q*(s,a)=1.
items.strategy: Track the empirical value of b and the unchanged optimistic value assigned to the unvisited action a.

items.title: The uninformative heuristic exposes the discount-factor powers
items.statement: Under U(s,a)=Vmax=1/(1-gamma), N_epsilon≤SA and sum_{s,a}[U(s,a)-V*(s)]_+≤SA/(1-gamma). For epsilon<1/(1-gamma), the R-MAX theorem therefore gives O-tilde(S^2 A/(epsilon^3(1-gamma)^6)), while the corrected Delayed Q-learning theorem gives O-tilde(SA/(epsilon^4(1-gamma)^8)). The O-tilde notation suppresses logarithmic factors.
items.strategy: Substitute the uninformative heuristic and its maximum gap into the two proved bounds and simplify powers.

items.title: Zero heuristic slack can still require one Delayed Q-learning update
items.statement: In a one-state MDP with gamma=0, actions a and b give deterministic rewards 1 and 0. Let U(a)=U(b)=V*(s)=1, Vmax=1, use a tie order selecting b first, and choose 0<epsilon1<1/2. Delayed Q-learning selects b for its first m samples and then lowers Q(s,b), although sum_{s,a}[U(s,a)-V*(s)]_+=0. Its finite bad-step cost is covered by the additive SA epsilon(1-gamma) term in the corrected bound.
items.strategy: Compute the initial tie, the first batch target, the update condition, and the heuristic-gap sum exactly.
